title: Gold in the fire clay
text: Ezra Hamilton owned a pottery in Los Angeles and made bricks and pipe from fire clay mined at Tropico Hill, near Willow Springs. In the 1890s he found gold in that clay, and a gold mine followed. The Tropico mill, built in the 1920s with a rotary ball mill circuit, was part of operations that generated about 50,000 tons of tailings. Glenn and Doreen Settle later turned the property into a Gold Camp, where a World Champion Gold Panning Contest was held each year.
